g4ela-25-1-morphology: Some word parts tell you where. Trans means across. Inter means between. Sub means under. Super means above or beyond. Put one in front of a word, and the word knows where it’s going. Find the part that tells where, then sew the border patch.
g4ela-25-2-grammar: A list needs commas so the reader can tell where one thing stops and the next begins. Rice, cotton, and corn. Without the commas, you might read rice cotton as one thing. Put a comma after every item but the last, and keep the one before and.
g4ela-25-3-spelling: Some mistakes slip past a spellchecker because they’re real words in the wrong place. Affect is the action. Effect is the result. It’s means it is. Its shows something belongs. When you’re not sure, say the long form out loud. If it sounds wrong, it is.
g4ela-25-4-grammar: Editing day. Read every list in your writing out loud. If you hear three things, you need two commas. A comma can change what a sentence means, so don’t guess. Ask how many things are in the list, then count your commas. One more slow read, and you’re ready to present.
